text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc said Friday it filed an application with the U.S. Department of Transportation seeking to operate flights with Transbrasil SA Linhas Aereas between the U.S. and several cities in Brazil.
Pending government approvals, the carriers propose starting service October 26.
Delta's application seeks approval to code share on daily service from Orlando, Miami, Washington D.C. and New York to Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Brasilia.
The application also seeks for approval to code share on connecting service to the following cities in Brazil: Porto Alegre, Florianopolis, Curitiba, Belo Horizonte, Fortaleza, Manaus, and Salvador.

Delta's application also requests the rights for Transbrasil to place its code on Delta flights from Cincinnati and Atlanta to Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, as well as on connecting service to Denver, Los Angeles, Chicago, Boston, Dallas/Fort Worth, Las Vegas, and Detroit.
Last month, the two carriers announced they had signed a letter of intent to pursue joint cooperation in marketing and others services, including code-share/blocked-space arrangements.
